headline: Both proxy and implementation verified on Etherscan; ChainSecurity + CertiK audits cover the deployed code; no implementation upgrade since 2019 deployment means zero post-audit drift.

findings.text: Proxy (AdminUpgradeabilityProxy, 0x45804880) is verified on Etherscan — 'Contract: Verified' per Etherscan search result, submitted 2019-08-29. Implementation (PAXGImplementation, 0x74271f2282) is separately verified on Etherscan with Compiler Version v0.4.24+commit.e67f0147, Optimization Enabled, MIT license. Etherscan explicitly labels the proxy as pointing to PAXGImplementation at 0x74271f2282 using OpenZeppelin's Unstructured Storage proxy pattern.

Public GitHub repo at github.com/paxosglobal/paxos-gold-contract exists and its README explicitly states 'The proxy contract and implementation contracts are verified on etherscan' at the pinned addresses. The repo contains contracts/, flattened/, and audit-reports/ directories. File structure and naming (PAXGImplementation) matches the Etherscan-visible contract name. No pinned commit SHA was obtained this run (GitHub tree fetch was blocked) — recorded in unknowns[].

GitHub README references two PAXG-specific audits: ChainSecurity (PDF at audit-reports/paxg-audits/ChainSecurity_PAXOS-GOLD.pdf) and CertiK formal verification (PDF at audit-reports/paxg-audits/CertiK_Verification_Report_for_Paxos.pdf). Both were conducted pre-deployment in 2019. The Paxos Standard (base code) was also audited by Nomic Labs, ChainSecurity, and Trail of Bits. The deployed implementation address (0x74271f2282) has not changed since the 2019 deployment, so the audited code IS the deployed code with no drift.

ChainSecurity and CertiK are both recognized security firms in the Solidity ecosystem. CertiK performed formal verification and static analysis. Trail of Bits (audited Paxos Standard base) is also a top-tier recognized firm. Both ChainSecurity and CertiK audits are directly linked from the official GitHub repo.

The repo has only 11 total commits (per GitHub page). The implementation contract address 0x74271f2282 has been the live implementation since contract deployment on 2019-08-29 (confirmed by proxy constructor argument decoded on Etherscan showing that same address). No upgradeTo() call has pointed to a different implementation — the defipunkd surfacer at block 25045950 shows implementation=0x74271F2282... consistent with original deployment. Therefore, no post-audit drift exists: the ChainSecurity and CertiK audits cover the exact bytecode currently deployed.

Both proxy and implementation are independently verified. Etherscan shows the proxy (AdminUpgradeabilityProxy) source code submitted 2019-08-29 and the implementation (PAXGImplementation) source code as a separate verified contract at 0x74271f2282, with full source including PAXGImplementation contract body visible in search results.

steelman.red: No audit URLs were pinned in the protocol context, and the audits are from 2019 — over 6 years ago — raising the question of whether any meaningful security review has occurred recently for a contract holding significant value.
steelman.orange: The audits predate the current analysis by 6+ years and the protocol has not published a follow-up audit since 2019; while the implementation is unchanged, new vulnerability classes discovered since 2019 (e.g., related to Solidity 0.4.x) have not been re-evaluated by a recognized firm.
steelman.green: Both proxy and implementation are verified on Etherscan, a public source repo exists whose contents match the deployed contracts, ChainSecurity and CertiK (both recognized firms) audited the PAXG-specific contracts pre-deployment, and the implementation address has not changed since 2019 — meaning the audited code is identically the deployed code with zero structural drift.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because both the proxy and implementation contracts are verified on Etherscan, the public GitHub repo at paxosglobal/paxos-gold-contract matches the deployed source, and two recognized firms (ChainSecurity and CertiK) audited the PAXG contracts pre-deployment. The implementation address (0x74271f2282) has been unchanged since the 2019 deployment as confirmed by the defipunkd surfacer and Etherscan constructor argument data — this means the audited code IS the deployed code with no post-audit drift whatsoever. The only note is the audit age (2019), but per the grade rubric, stale-audit is an orange downgrade only when drift exists; here there is no drift because no upgrade has occurred.

protocol_metadata.about: Paxos Gold (PAXG) is an ERC-20 token on Ethereum where each token represents one fine troy ounce of an LBMA-certified London Good Delivery gold bar held in Brink's vaults in London under the custody of Paxos Trust Company. Users can purchase, transfer, and redeem PAXG for physical gold, unallocated gold, or USD through the Paxos platform. The token uses an AdminUpgradeabilityProxy pattern (ZeppelinOS) with a single supplyController that mints and burns tokens based on gold movements, an assetProtectionRole that can freeze/seize addresses per regulatory requirements, and a configurable fee mechanism for on-chain transfers. Paxos is regulated by the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) and publishes monthly gold attestation reports.
